There are 4 parallel sets of the reactor to cater to the large volume of BF gas, considering the 50% turndown operation design. The CO-content at the outlet of the high temperature (HT) Shift Reactor (R01 A/B/C/D) is approx. 3.8 to 4 mol% (dry). The heat generated by the system is used to generate steam and preheat BFW in the downstream equipment. The main parameters to be controlled in the CO shift reactor are the S: DG ratio (to maintain the forward reaction and avoid endothermic reverse WGS reaction) and the inlet temperature of the reactor. A steam-to-dry gas ratio of 0.5 (at the exit of the WGS reactor) is achieved by flow control of the process steam to the system. WGS boiler (E01A/B) operation control is done via three element control philosophy, where steam flow is measured together with boiler drum level and feed water flow. The drum level controller manipulates the feed water flow SP in conjunction with steam flow measurement (Feed Forward Control). The Feed Forward Attachment-7: Initial Engineering Design and Cost Estimate 9 DE-FE0031937 / 0009 Control keeps the feed water supply balanced with the steam demand. The drum level controller trims the feed water flow SP to compensate for errors in the flow measurements or any other unmeasured load disturbances (e.g. blowdown) that may affect the drum level. In the BFW Preheater (E02A/B), BFW is heated with hot Shift Gas exiting the WGS Boiler. The level in Steam Drum controls the flow to BFW Preheater. The temperature of the process gas is controlled by the BFW flow bypass across the two parallel sets of the exchanger. The preheater exchanger reduces the temperature from 365°F to 250°F. Process gas travels from bottom to top releases heat, and cools from 839°F to 365°F. BFW enters at a temperature of 293°F and comes out as saturated steam converted to superheated steam after passing through the BFW Superheater. The cooled shifted gas from the BFW pre-heater is further cooled in the quench tower (C01) to maintain a lower temperature before entering the CCU island. The cooling of the shifted gas to 91°F is controlled via the recirculation rate of the process condensate in the Quench Tower (C01). The level of the tower is controlled by the level controller placed at the sump through which the net positive suction head is maintained for the process condensate pump. The temperature of the cooled shifted gas sends a signal to the condensate export's flow controller, ensuring sufficient recirculation flow. The partial cold blowdown flow control is connected to the sump level controller. 4.0 Carbon Capture Unit 4.1 Design Basis ION Clean Energy (ION) has developed the Carbon Capture System (CCS) that removes 95% CO from blast 2 furnace gas under normal operating conditions.
